title: ⭐ Practice: one form at a time

questions.prompt: Complete: "Last summer they ___ the whole journey in one evening."
questions.explanation: "Last summer" is a finished past time, so we need the simple past. The verb plan ends in a short vowel and one consonant, so that consonant doubles before -ed: "planned". "planed" keeps a single n, "plans" is a present form, and "planning" cannot stand alone without an auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Complete: "She didn't ___ the office before eight o'clock yesterday."
questions.explanation: After didn't the verb goes back to its base form, which gives didn't "leave". "left" is the simple past, and the past is already carried by didn't; "leaves" is a present form; and "leaving" needs an auxiliary such as was in front of it.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Did the manager ___ about the new contract?"
questions.explanation: In a past question, Did is followed by the subject and the base verb, so the form is "know". "knew" repeats a past that Did already marks, "known" is the past participle used with have or has, and "knows" is a present form.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My uncle ___ a lot of money from his small bakery."
questions.explanation: No time is stated and the result counts today, so the sentence needs the present perfect: has + past participle, which gives "has made". "have made" does not agree with the singular subject My uncle, "has make" keeps the base form after has, and "has maked" invents a regular form for an irregular verb.

questions.prompt: Complete: "In twelve years of business, I ___ lost a single client."
questions.explanation: The markers ever, never, already and just stand between have/has and the participle, so the order is "have never" lost. "have ever" picks the wrong marker: ever belongs to questions — Have you ever lost a client? — not to an affirmative statement; "has never" does not agree with the subject I, and "haven't never" builds a double negative.

questions.prompt: Complete the short answer: "Has your sister found a flat?" — "No, she ___."
questions.explanation: A short answer repeats the auxiliary of the question. The question opens with Has and the subject is she, so the reply is "hasn't". "haven't" belongs to I, you, we and they; "didn't" replies to a question that opens with Did, and "doesn't" replies to one that opens with Does.
